questions.text: Let N be an NFA with n states. Let k be the number of states of a minimal DFA which is equivalent to N. Which one of the following is necessarily true?
questions.solution:
The subset construction turns an n-state NFA into a DFA whose states are subsets of the NFA's states, at most [latex]2^n[/latex]. The minimal DFA cannot be bigger, but it can be much smaller (so the other bounds are not guaranteed).

Answer: [latex]k\le2^n[/latex]

questions.text: The set of all recursively enumerable languages is
questions.solution:
RE languages are closed under intersection (run both TMs; accept when both accept). They are not closed under complement, are a superset (not subset) of recursive languages, and are countable (TMs can be listed).

Answer: closed under intersection

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
questions.solution:
Type checking is part of semantic analysis, which comes after parsing (it needs the syntax tree). So "type checking is done before parsing" is false. The other statements are true.

Answer: Type checking is done before parsing

questions.text:
The following are some events that occur after a device controller issues an interrupt while process L is under execution.
(P) The processor pushes the process status of L onto the control stack.
(Q) The processor finishes the execution of the current instruction.
(R) The processor executes the interrupt service routine.
(S) The processor pops the process status of L from the control stack.
(T) The processor loads the new PC value based on the interrupt.
Which one of the following is the correct order in which the events above occur?
questions.solution:
Order of interrupt handling:
Q: finish the current instruction [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P: save L's status on the stack [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T: load the PC with the ISR address [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R: run the ISR [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S: restore L's status.

Answer: QPTRS

questions.text:
Consider a process executing on an operating system that uses demand paging. The average time for a memory access in the system is M units if the corresponding memory page is available in memory, and D units if the memory access causes a page fault. It has been experimentally measured that the average time taken for a memory access in the process is X units.
Which one of the following is the correct expression for the page fault rate experienced by the process?
questions.solution:
With page fault rate p: [latex]X=(1-p)M+pD=M+p(D-M)[/latex].

[latex]p=\frac{X-M}{D-M}[/latex]

Answer: (X - M) / (D - M)
